title: Espresso shift bullet log — kv-prefetch leak & canary rollback plan
content:
Quick context:
- Morning canary (kv-prefetch-enabled) rolled out to 10% of requests on dedicated pool `dp-west-3`.
- After ~90m we saw a steady rise in per-container RSS (~+1.1GB) on the canary nodes; non-canary nodes stable.
- P95 latency unchanged; P99 spiked intermittently during GC stutters.
- Canary now at 0% (manual rollback) but need root-cause + short-term mitigations + reliable repro for patch.

Observations (raw):
- Heap profile snapshots (saved at 10:05, 11:20, 12:00) show increased growth in `kv_prefetch::prefetch_buffers` and `kv_cache::sharded_maps` objects.
- Number of outstanding prefetch futures climbs with request concurrency > 120.
- GC frequency increased on nodes running newer kernel build (nvml/allocator tweak merged yesterday).
- Containers with 24h uptime show leak; fresh containers (recreated) start at baseline then diverge after ~30m under load.

Repro steps (local minimal):
1) Start small runtime binary with feature flag `--kv-prefetch=true` and `--prefetch-max-inflight=2048`
2) Run workload: wrk2 style steady-state with 150 concurrent connections, seq len 320, tokens/use ~350
3) Observe rss via `docker stats` or `kubectl top pod` every 60s; capture pprof heap at minute 15/30/45
4) Confirm growth pattern matches canary logs

Commands/snippets to capture profiles quickly:
- curl -sS http://$POD:6060/debug/pprof/heap > heap-$(date +%s).prof
- kubectl exec -n runtime $POD -- sh -c 'ps aux | grep runtime && cat /proc/$MAIN_PID/status' > proc-status.txt
- /opt/runtime/bin/runtime --log-level=debug --kv-prefetch=true --prefetch-max-inflight=512

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Prefetch buffer accounting bug: prefetch buffer entries not freed on cache eviction path when requests are cancelled (most likely)
B) Interaction with new allocator: small-object allocator change causes slower free path, GC thrash triggers retention of prefetched blocks
C) Leak only manifests under high concurrency due to a race in inflight-futures bookkeeping
D) Unrelated: client-side retries cause prepended duplicate prefetches (less likely, but check client traces)

Immediate mitigations (fast, reversible):
- Roll canary to 0% (done) and stop autoscale from placing extra canary pods.
- Add server-side guard: cap per-request prefetch to 128 when pod uptime > 20m (hotfix toggle).
- Add aggressive periodic free pass: trigger `kv_cache.compact()` every 10m as emergency (observed to reduce RSS but is a bandaid).

Planned experiments (this afternoon):
1) Reproduce locally with small binary + high concurrency; iterate on prefetch cancellation path with logging: add counters for alloc/free of prefetch buffers. (Me / Rajiv) ETA 3h
2) Run A/B: canary with `--prefetch-max-inflight=512` vs `2048` and measure gain. (Mina) ETA end of day
3) Microbenchmark allocator free path on patched allocator commit and compare with previous build. (Me) ETA 24h
4) Fuzz cancellation sequence: send STREAM-CANCEL after request token N, ensure prefetch future cancellation flows through dealloc path. (Rajiv/Mina) ETA 6h

Metrics to collect (add to observability quick dashboard):
- per-pod: rss, heap-alloc, num-prefetch-inflight, num-prefetch-allocs, num-prefetch-frees, gc-pauses-ms
- route-level: average inflight futures per-request, cancellation rate, average tokens requested via prefetch
- alert: if rss growth > 400MB in 30m with no corresponding user traffic increase -> auto page

Acceptance criteria for fix: (must be measurable)
- Under 4h steady-state at 150 concurrency, rss delta < 150MB across 3 pod restarts
- p99 latency not degraded by more than 5% vs baseline
- prefetched buffers freed count >= alloc count within 60s of request completion in pprof traces

To-dos (who / ETA):
- Add lightweight alloc/free counters to `kv_prefetch` (Me) - PR draft by EOD 2026-03-12
- Add dashboard panels for `prefetch_allocs` / `prefetch_frees` (Mina) - WIP, ETA 2026-03-13
- Create JIRA SRV-1173 with reproducer steps and attach heap profiles (Me) - created (link above)
- Try canary with lowered inflight cap 512 (Rajiv) - request queued for 11:30
- Schedule 30m sync with alloc owner (Theo) and Mina to review profiler output (Me) - 15:00

Notes to self / heuristics:
- If leak requires full restart to recover, we probably lack a safe eviction path; consider adding pod-lifecycle job that drains prefetch queues before SIGTERM
- Keep hotfix surface minimal: prefer config caps over code paths until repro confirmed
- Remember: p99 spikes can be GC or kernel scheduling; correlate with `dmesg` and `node_exporter` sched metrics

Meeting snippet (pair with Mina @15:00):
- Bring heap profiles, two flamegraphs (before/after canary rollback), sample logs showing inflight futures count for a slow request
- Agenda: reproduce -> confirm alloc/free mismatch -> propose fix (counter + safe free) -> roll plan

Follow-ups / backlog ideas (later):
- Add automated leak-detection smoke tests to CI that run a 30m prefetched workload in a sandbox and assert rss slope < threshold
- Consider adding weak pointers or TTL to prefetch buffers so stale buffers drop automatically after Xs
- Explore per-tenant prefetch knobs in dedicated pools for noisy tenants

Random scratch notes: 
- Observed odd log: `WARN prefetch cancelled but buffer not found id=0x7fa1b2` — grep across canary logs to collect instances
- Check PR #4818 (allocator tweak) for comments referencing small-object list glue

End of log. Short nap then debugging sprint.

-- Priyanka
